Bishop’s University offers both a thesis-based and a course-based Master of Science (MSc) in Physics. The course-based Master’s program provides a strong academic foundation for students pursuing professional careers, while the thesis-based Master’s program emphasizes research excellence and serves as an entry point for students interested in doctoral studies, as well as those seeking research-oriented professional paths. Many graduates of the thesis-based program continue on to PhD studies, while others have successfully transitioned directly into professional careers upon completion of their degree.

Admission to the thesis-based Master’s program is contingent upon the availability of a faculty member willing to supervise the candidate’s research and academic program. Prospective students are encouraged to consult the Faculty section to identify potential supervisors. While preliminary contact with potential supervisors is not required, it is strongly recommended.

The central component of the thesis-based MSc program is the dissertation. Under the guidance of a supervisor, students conduct original research leading to the development of a thesis. The program culminates in the submission of a written dissertation that supports the thesis, followed by an oral defense before an examination committee.
